title: Preservation of compatible scalar endomorphisms
statement: Let C have object universe c and morphism universe v, let k=max(c,v,r), suppose C is essentially small in k, let J be a Grothendieck topology on C, let U be an object, and let B_n be a tower of commutative ring sheaves with adjacent maps τ_n:B_(n+1)→B_n. Use the actual systems, coefficient maps, evaluations and scalar restrictions of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. Every ordinary open datum O [def-pur-sequence-site-open-data] satisfies Scalars [def-pur-sequence-open-derived-data]: for every commutative ring R, natural section maps R→B_n(X) compatible with all coefficient maps, t∈R, and localized system M, multiplication by t defines the prescribed sectionwise endomorphisms f of M and g of O.Jfun(M), and O.Jfun(f)=g.

proof.text: Compatible sections define multiplication endomorphisms on the actual module over the sequence ring. Commutativity gives linearity; naturality and compatibility with every composite tower map give the restriction equation. The localized composite coefficient maps agree with the restrictions of the ambient maps, by the naturality of the identity transformation of op-sequence functors.

To show level extension preserves multiplication, transpose along [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]; naturality of the unit reduces the equation to linearity of the unit component. Apply naturality of O.level to the scalar endomorphism and use this equation. Each level comparison is invertible, so its section map is injective; cancellation gives the actual system equality.
